notes: Six cases, 4 categories, 3 difficulty levels. No secrets or personal data. References are official documentation pages whose URLs returned HTTP 200 when checked on 2026-10-15; reaching a page does NOT mean any generated question has been verified against it. Factual accuracy is a manual review against the rubric and references (see manual_review_template.json).

cases.category_description: Testez les fondamentaux du langage, les collections et les pratiques Python.
cases.learning_objective: Built-in collections (list, tuple, dict, set) and their basic operations.
cases.rubric: Each question must be answerable from the cited tutorial page; exactly one choice correct; no Python-version-specific claim unless stated.

cases.category_description: Testez les fondamentaux du langage, les collections et les pratiques Python.
cases.learning_objective: Classes, instance vs class attributes, and subtle object-model behaviour.
cases.rubric: Subtle cases must be decidable from the cited page; reject questions relying on unstated interpreter behaviour.

cases.category_description: Explorez les modèles, les vues, les API et les tests avec Django.
cases.learning_objective: Django models: fields, relationships and what a model represents.
cases.rubric: Answers must agree with the cited model documentation of the stable Django release.

cases.category_description: Explorez les modèles, les vues, les API et les tests avec Django.
cases.learning_objective: QuerySets: filtering, lazy evaluation and common query patterns.
cases.rubric: Answers must agree with the cited queries documentation; reject invented ORM methods.

cases.category_description: Mettez en pratique les composants, les hooks et les interfaces React.
cases.learning_objective: useState and useEffect: state updates and effect dependencies.
cases.rubric: Answers must agree with the cited react.dev reference pages; reject class-component-only or deprecated guidance.

cases.category_description: Progressez sur les types, le narrowing et les fonctionnalités TypeScript.
cases.rubric: Answers must agree with the cited handbook page; code snippets must be valid TypeScript.
